reference_fields: Raspberry and Blackberry Varieties for Maine

categories.name: Red raspberries, everbearing
categories.description: primocane-fruiting, listed by fall ripening date, earliest-latest

categories.name: Purple raspberries, summer-bearing
categories.description: In general, purple raspberries are not adequately hardy to be commercially viable in most of Maine.

categories.name: Black raspberries
categories.description: Black raspberries may winter-kill to the snowline if temperatures drop to -10 degrees F. They are also quite susceptible to virus infections, Verticillium, anthracnose, and rust. They are not considered commercially viable for Maine.

categories.name: Blackberries, thorny
categories.description: erect Erect blackberries have tall, rugged canes with prominent thorns. They are sensitive to low temperatures (-10 degrees or colder) and are therefore not recommended for commercial production in Maine. Virus infections are common in blackberries and may cause poor winter survival and sterility, resulting in no fruit.

categories.name: Blackberries, thornless
categories.description: Thornless blackberries have vigorous canes that must be staked or trellised. They tend to be more sensitive to winter injury than thorny varieties and are not hardy below -10 degrees F. They should only be planted in sites protected from wind and extreme cold. They are not considered commercially viable for Maine. They ripen later than most red raspberries.

categories.name: Blackberries, everbearing
categories.description: Fall crop ripens too late to be practical in Maine
